problem: Prior VLN navigators and speakers use LSTMs to carry information flow, which handle cross-modal interaction well but neglect intra-modal interactions. Directly applying a standard Transformer to VLN has also been unsatisfactory.
motivation: Both the navigator and the speaker (instruction generator used for data augmentation) limit VLN performance. Better modeling of intra-modal relations, for example among words or among views, could improve both.
key_idea: Replace LSTM information flow in both the VLN navigator and the speaker with Transformer-style multi-head self-attention plus residual connections, and add a switch in the navigator to control what enters the information flow directly.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that intra-modal self-attention combined with a gated (switched) residual path is what makes Transformers work in VLN, where a plain Transformer had underperformed.
method: Transformer-based navigator: multi-head self-attention with residual connections carries the information flow in place of an LSTM.
Switch mechanism: a gate in the navigator that prevents certain inputs from entering the information flow directly through the residual path.
Transformer-based speaker: multi-head self-attention with residual connections for generating instructions from routes.

setting.backbone: Transformer-based navigator and speaker (trained; details not given in the abstract)
setting.training_data: not stated in the abstract (presumably R2R with speaker-based augmentation)

results: The abstract claims significant performance advantages over baselines but gives no numbers.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the evaluation details and results could not be verified.
The Transformer replaces LSTM but the paper likely remains confined to the standard R2R discrete setting.
